question: For how many (not necessarily positive) integer values of \(n\) is the value of \[ 4000 \cdot \left(\tfrac{2}{5}\right)^n \] an integer?
solution:
The expression involves only the primes \(2\) and \(5\), so track their exponents. Since \(4000=2^5\cdot5^3\),
\[
4000\left(\frac25\right)^n=2^{5+n}5^{3-n}.
\]
Because \(2\) and \(5\) are distinct primes, a negative exponent would leave an uncanceled prime factor in the denominator. Thus the value is an integer exactly when
\[
5+n\ge0\qquad\text{and}\qquad3-n\ge0,
\]
which gives \(-5\le n\le3\). Including both endpoints, there are
\[
3-(-5)+1=9
\]
such integers. The answer is \(\boxed{9}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
